title: Fertilizer by Area Calculator: Grams per m²
description: Total up fertilizer from a label rate in grams per square metre with the Fertilizer by Area Calculator — area × rate, in kg. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a 500 m² garden at a label rate of 25 g/m² needs exactly 12.5 kg of product — one bag, not the two the guesswork usually buys.
quick_answer: The Fertilizer by Area Calculator multiplies a treatment area by a product's label rate in grams per square metre and returns the total product needed, in kilograms and grams. Enter the area and the rate on the bag and it does the multiplication between a label and a purchase.

My rate is in pounds per 1,000 sq ft. Can I use it?
Convert first: 1 lb per 1,000 sq ft ≈ 4.88 g/m². US lawn labels use the imperial rate; this calculator's unit is the metric label's. The conversion factor is the bridge.
What if my area is in square feet?
Divide sq ft by 10.7639 for m², or note the worked conversion in the examples — a 1,000 sq ft lawn is about 92.9 m².
Compute each bed separately and add the totals. One blended rate across different products is how beds get the wrong feed.
Why grams per square metre on labels?
Because it makes the purchase arithmetic trivial at garden scale and scales cleanly to hectares (1 g/m² = 10 kg/ha) for the same product's farm life.
My lawn is an odd shape.
Split it into rectangles and circles you can measure, total the areas, then run one calculation. Odd shapes are just several honest shapes added together.
